newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down in line with CBOT soybeans.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down in line with CBOT soybeans.

text.p: WCE canola futures settled lower, pressured by a weaker CBOT soy complex and the strong Canadian dollar, traders said.
"Lack of export interest was also noted," a trader said. "We have seen hedges and general commercial selling amid the prevailing weaker tone to the market."
Flax ended up on some commercial buying coupled with light hedges, the trader said. January canola lost $0.40 at $402.10 a tonne and January flax gained $1.40 at $351.20.
February western barley firmed $0.40 at $136.80 and March feed wheat gained $3.40 at $173.40.

Barley was aided by some commission house and commercial buying. "I think what is lending support is the cold weather in the prairies," another trader said. News that Saudi Arabia bought 1.2 million tonnes of optional-origin barley which may include Canadian barley already was factored in the market, he said.

He also noted talk of the lack of nearby feed wheat for delivery against the board. Oats were bid up by commission houses with no trade. March oats settled up $US2.00 to $US117.00 and May feed peas dropped $US1.00 to $US191.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
